title: Accessible React UI primitives
summary: Build accessible, themeable React interfaces from unstyled primitives: dialogs, menus, popovers, tabs, forms, tables, date/time and drag-and-drop. Compare React Aria, Base UI, Radix, Headless UI, Ark UI and Ariakit; styled design systems are reference alternatives.
constraints: Permissive license across the full dependency tree
Accessible primitives with keyboard, focus management and ARIA semantics
Unstyled or minimally styled primitives; no required CSS-in-JS runtime
Actively maintained: a release within 12 months
No unfixed high or critical advisories
No install scripts in the dependency tree
Client-only rendering is acceptable; React Server Components are not required
If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap
out_of_scope: Visual design, theming and brand tokens
Choosing a date library or data-grid vendor
notes: This requirement is for headless or minimally styled primitives, not a finished design system. Styled systems such as Mantine, Chakra UI, MUI, Ant Design, HeroUI, Fluent UI and React Spectrum S2 are reference alternatives and are not reviewed here as headless options. React Aria Components is the component layer; react-aria and react-stately are the lower-level hooks and state packages beneath it. Base UI is the renamed @base-ui/react package; @base-ui-components/react is deprecated. Ariakit is the renamed @ariakit/react package. Radix UI is distributed both as the unified radix-ui package and as individual @radix-ui/react-* packages.
